gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Megrim looks angular and futuristic, with every stroke ending at one measured thickness and a c bent open like a paperclip. Noto Sans Ethiopic is the sturdier one, built for steady reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Futuristic and angular, Megrim looks like neatly bent pipe cleaner. Its job is turning heads with that wiry display texture, while Noto Sans Georgian handles the reading with open curves and short ascender stems.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Megrim draws every stroke at a single weight, angular and futuristic. It excels at striking display lettering, whereas Noto Sans Glagolitic stays approachable, its round letters staying clear at small sizes.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Not one stroke in Megrim ever thins out, so the letters feel measured and angular. That makes it a striking display face, while Noto Sans Gothic does the reading work with big counters and round forms like open parentheses.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Futuristic is the first word for Megrim, where even the crossbars match the stems in thickness and the c gapes open. Noto Sans Grantha handles the quieter job, and its flattened pen-nib bowls never snag the eye while reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Megrim has a tube-like stroke that resembles neon glass, angular and futuristic from end to end. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi sits beneath it with chunky crayon-mark lowercase and terminals cut back to leave a big gap.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-hk: Sharp, wiry and futuristic, Megrim looks drawn with one pen tip, every glyph kept to the same simple line. Noto Sans HK feels plainer and larger beside it, brush ends lifting away.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-jp: Futuristic through and through, Megrim has no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, just angular strokes with a skyward x-height line. Noto Sans JP, with sweeping open curves, would read smoothly and modern over paragraphs.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean and modern, with generous openings like chisel notches and small letters standing almost capital-sized. Megrim above it looks bent from one length of wire, so give it the larger size.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads approachable, its gaping curves and lofty small letters easy to follow. Megrim's strength is thin joins no thinner than its stems, a wiry display look, while the sans handles the text.
